desc:
Numbers arrive one at a time in the order of nums. After each arrival, compute the median of all numbers received so far. The median of an odd count is the middle value of the sorted numbers; the median of an even count is the average of the two middle values.

To keep every answer an integer, report twice the median: for an odd count that is 2 * middle, for an even count it is the sum of the two middle values. Return the reports for every prefix.

nums = [5, 2, 8, 1]
[5]        -> median 5   -> 10
[2, 5]     -> median 3.5 -> 7
[2, 5, 8]  -> median 5   -> 10
[1,2,5,8]  -> median 3.5 -> 7
answer = [10, 7, 10, 7]
constraints: Each reported value fits in a 32-bit signed integer
hints: Re-sorting every prefix costs O(n<sup>2</sup> log n); inserting into a sorted list is still O(n) per step. You only need the middle.
Split the numbers seen so far into a lower half and an upper half. The median lives at the boundary between them.

Keep a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, with sizes differing by at most one (lower half gets the extra). Insert into the correct side, then rebalance by moving one root across.
editorial: Maintain two heaps: lo is a max-heap (stored as negated values in a min-heap library) holding the smaller half, and hi is a min-heap holding the larger half. Invariant: every value in lo is ≤ every value in hi, and len(lo) is either len(hi) or len(hi) + 1.

For a new value x: if lo is empty or x ≤ max(lo), push into lo, else into hi. Then rebalance: if lo has two more elements than hi, move the root of lo to hi; if hi has more than lo, move the root of hi to lo.

With an odd count the median is the root of lo (report twice it); with an even count it is the average of the two roots, so the doubled report is just their sum. Each step is O(log n), and the roots give the middle in O(1). The doubled median is at most 2 * 109 in absolute value, which still fits in a signed 32-bit integer.
